narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (1D CNN) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (1,112 subjects, 539 ASD/573 TD, 17 sites), reduced to 871 subjects after CPAC preprocessing QC (a separate statement reports 505 ASD/530 TD as the dataset used).
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC/PCP-preprocessed functional connectivity (CC400 atlas) fed into a 1D CNN; compared against optimised SVM, KNN and Random Forest; evaluated via 10-fold CV and a leave-site-out scheme across all 17 sites.
narrative_rows.outcomes: CNN achieved 70.22% 10-fold CV accuracy, outperforming SVM (69%), KNN (62%) and RF (60%); leave-site-out accuracy varied by site, exceeding 70% at KKI, SDSU and USM.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Exact ASD/TD split of the final 871-subject analysed sample not stated; no numeric motion/FD cut-off given; data available only on request, not openly released; within-fold leakage control for hyperparameter tuning not described.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Combines a standard pooled 10-fold CV evaluation with an explicit leave-site-out analysis across all 17 ABIDE I sites, making site-level generalisation directly reportable for the dataset-publication link.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (SVM on combined structural-texture and functional-ICA features) using ABIDE I (1111 scans, 573 HC/538 ASD, 17 sites), split 800 training / 311 hold-out test (case:control ratio preserved).
narrative_rows.methods: SPM8-preprocessed structural and resting-state fMRI; structural texture features from a sparse-autoencoder convolutional model and functional features from subject-level spatial ICA time courses, combined via linear SVM (LEFMSF); 5-fold CV for hyperparameter tuning within the training set, evaluated on an untouched hold-out set; explicit site-confound checks.
narrative_rows.outcomes: LEFMSF achieved 0.643 hold-out accuracy on ABIDE (specificity 0.683, sensitivity 0.600), the best known result using imaging data alone at publication, exceeding prior work by 0.042; a site-only baseline classifier scored only 55.0% and a site-balanced re-test gave 63.46%, arguing against a site-driven result.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No named ROI atlas/standard connectivity pipeline (features are ICA/texture-based); no motion/FD-based QC rule reported; diagnostic label source not described; exact ASD/TD counts within the hold-out test set not individually reported.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A methodologically careful example combining structural and functional ABIDE I features with an explicit, quantitative check that model performance is not driven by site identity, directly relevant to confound/leakage assessment in ABIDE-based prediction studies.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (deep transfer learning) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI from four target sites (UM n=113: 48 ASD/65 healthy; UCLA n=75: 36/39; USM n=61: 38/23; LEUVEN n=61: 27/34), with offline SSAE pretraining on healthy subjects from the remaining 16 ABIDE sites.
narrative_rows.methods: CCS-preprocessed functional connectivity (AAL atlas, 90 ROIs) with site/age/gender/handedness regressed out via OLS; a stacked sparse autoencoder pretrained offline on non-target-site healthy subjects, transferred into a DTL-NN classifier and compared against DNN and SVM baselines via stratified 5-fold CV per site.
narrative_rows.outcomes: DTL-NN outperformed DNN and SVM at every site, with the best performance at USM (70.4% accuracy, 0.73 AUC) and an average of 67.1% accuracy/0.71 AUC across sites, significantly better than DNN for accuracy (p=0.03) and sensitivity (p=0.04).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No motion/FD-based QC threshold or pipeline version reported; diagnostic label source not described; no code/participant-list availability statement; small per-site sample sizes (61-113).
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a transfer-learning design that explicitly separates offline pretraining data (non-target ABIDE sites) from target-site evaluation data, alongside an explicit site-covariate regression, both directly relevant to site-leakage assessment in ABIDE-based prediction studies.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) analysis using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (584 datasets: 278 ASD/306 TD, nine sites) as an independent replication of an original 15 ASD/15 TD task+resting-state sample.
narrative_rows.methods: Seed-based intrinsic functional connectivity of the right posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS), computed with the same in-house SPM-based procedure as the original sample; mean FD included as a nuisance covariate, with a motion-scrubbed secondary analysis; small-volume and whole-brain FWE-corrected statistics.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ABIDE replication confirmed reduced pSTS connectivity with right IPL, left premotor area, fusiform gyrus and bilateral superior occipital gyrus in ASD (replicating the original sample), plus increased pSTS connectivity with left thalamus and right IFG not seen in the original sample.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No named/versioned standard connectivity pipeline or atlas used for the ABIDE data (seed-based, in-house SPM procedure); no code/participant-list availability statement; cross-site IQ not matched.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An early (2013) example of using the full multi-site ABIDE release as an independent large-sample replication cohort for a seed-based connectivity finding from a small original sample, with an explicit motion (FD covariate + scrubbing) sensitivity analysis.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ensemble SVM) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI from subjects sharing one scan protocol, n=84 (45 ASD/39 TC) after excluding 23 subjects for excessive motion.
narrative_rows.methods: DPARSF-preprocessed functional connectivity (AAL atlas, 90 ROIs, 4,005 edges) plus graph-theory metrics, classified with a random cluster of 500 bootstrap/feature-subsampled SVMs (majority vote), evaluated on a single 70/30 train/test split.
narrative_rows.outcomes: The random SVM cluster achieved 96.15% test accuracy with an optimal 272-feature subset, far exceeding a single SVM; discriminative regions included inferior frontal gyrus, hippocampus, precuneus and cingulate gyrus.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Headline accuracy is derived from a single train/test split in which both the ensemble size and the feature-set dimensionality were tuned by maximising accuracy on that same test set, with no cross-validation or independent validation set; diagnostic label source not described; no code/participant-list availability statement; small, single-protocol sample.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A cautionary example for the review: the very high reported accuracy (96.15%) on a small single-protocol ABIDE subset is attributable to test-set leakage during hyperparameter/feature-set selection rather than independently validated generalisation performance.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (3D-CNN on voxel-wise rs-fMRI summary measures) using combined ABIDE I+II (N=2,085 after a minimum scan-duration QC cutoff; 993 ASD, 1,092 TD; 29 institutions).
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed voxel-wise temporal summary measures (ReHo, ALFF, fALFF, degree/eigenvector centrality, LFCD, entropy, VMHC, autocorrelation lag) fed into per-measure and ensemble/combined 3D-CNN models and linear-SVM equivalents; evaluated via five-fold CV and a separate leave-site-out CV across the five largest sites.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best model (MM-ensemble) reached 64% balanced accuracy/66% F1 under five-fold CV, comparable to the single ReHo measure, but dropped to 56% balanced accuracy/59% F1 under leave-site-out CV, generalising well only to the NYU site.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No motion/FD-based QC threshold reported (only a scan-duration cutoff); no atlas/ROI parcellation used; diagnostic label source not described; large drop in performance under leave-site-out evaluation indicates limited cross-site generalisation.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A methodologically strong example directly quantifying the gap between pooled cross-validation and leave-site-out generalisation on combined ABIDE I+II, with openly released code, highly relevant to assessing site-generalisation claims in ABIDE-based prediction studies.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (SVM on graph-theoretical features) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI, 816 individuals across 22 sites, stratified into five age groups (exact ASD/HC split reported only in a supplementary table).
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC/PCP-preprocessed functional connectivity (AAL atlas, 116 ROIs; multiple connectivity measures) summarised into 817 graph-theoretical features, reduced to 10 via sequential feature selection and classified with a linear SVM per age group; evaluated via 10-fold CV with 10x10 Welch's t-test model comparisons (FDR-corrected).
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best model (>30 years age group) achieved ~95% accuracy, 97% sensitivity, 95% specificity; centrality measures were the most consistently informative features across age groups.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: ASD/HC split not available in the extracted full text (only in a supplementary table); no numeric motion/FD threshold reported; unclear whether feature selection was confined to training folds; no site covariate/harmonisation across the pooled multi-site sample; data available only on request, not openly deposited.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An age-stratified ABIDE I analysis demonstrating that graph-theoretical centrality features combined with careful overfitting controls (linear kernel, few features, 10-fold CV) can achieve high accuracy in an older-age ASD subgroup, though feature-selection leakage risk is not fully resolved by the reported methods.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs TC); ABIDE I preprocessed-connectomes-project release; 872 of 1112 subjects, 20 sites
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs); population-graph convolutional neural network ensemble (bootstrapped G-CNN) trained with edge dropout and compared against a single G-CNN and linear SVM baseline; 10-fold cross-validation matching a prior study's splits and code.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Bootstrapped G-CNN reached 70.86% accuracy (graph condition), outperforming the baseline G-CNN (69.50%) and linear SVM (66.8%), with improved robustness (67.85%/67.39%) under naive or noisy population graphs versus baseline (66.93%/66.35%).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No stated motion/QC threshold, no diagnosis-source statement, no leakage or site-handling description, single-split accuracy without confidence intervals.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a predictive, ABIDE-I-only, CPAC/Harvard-Oxford population-graph classification approach; cohort subset is a fixed N (872/1112) without a published selection rule.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) mega-analysis; ABIDE I (369 autism/481 NT) and ABIDE II (205 autism/347 NT) combined with EU-AIMS LEAP (222/200) for a total of 796 autism/1028 NT across 32 sites
narrative_rows.methods: Pearson-correlation connectomes from Schaefer-400 cortical + 15 Harvard-Oxford subcortical ROIs; ComBat site harmonisation; per-edge GLM with diagnosis, age, sex, mean FD covariates assessed with the Network-Based Statistic at FWE-corrected thresholds; canonical correlation analysis linking connectivity to clinical symptom dimensions.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Autism showed brain-wide hypoconnectivity (13,001 edges, 17.1% of edges, pfwe<0.001), concentrated in sensory/somatomotor/attention networks, and hyperconnectivity (16,767 edges, 22% of edges, pfwe<0.001), concentrated in DMN/subcortical connections; pattern replicated separately in LEAP and in combined ABIDE I/II data.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Preprocessing pipeline name/version and exact exclusion criteria are deferred to a supplement not present in the extracted full text; analysis excluded the cerebellum due to poor scan coverage; most participants under 25 years old; sex ratio imbalanced between groups.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A large multi-site mega-analysis explicitly reporting ABIDE I and ABIDE II subsample sizes separately and replicating its connectome-wide findings within the combined ABIDE I/II data alone.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs HC); ABIDE used as a secondary validation dataset alongside ADNI; release, N and sites not reported in available text
narrative_rows.methods: Diffusion-based generative brain-network construction (Brain Region Alignment Module, a DDPM-based registration network) combined with a graph-contrastive Brain Network Optimization Module (GCN-based), compared against brain networks built with the PANDA toolbox; five-fold cross-validation stated generically for the model.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ROI attention scores identified somatomotor network (SMN) connectivity and DMN-DAN/DMN-FPN connectivity as most important for ASD prediction; on ABIDE the proposed method's constructed networks had higher reliability (ICC 0.71 vs 0.64) and much lower construction time than PANDA; no numeric ASD classification accuracy/AUC table is present in the extracted text.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: ABIDE cohort N, sites, release, diagnosis source, preprocessing pipeline and atlas are not reported; no quantitative ASD classification performance table (unlike the detailed ADNI 5-fold results in Table 5); authors note the model cannot explain pathogenesis and the dataset used is relatively small.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Illustrates a predictive deep-learning paper where ABIDE is a secondary, thinly-documented validation dataset; useful as a negative example for cohort/pipeline reporting completeness in the knowledge graph.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs TC); ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project release (ABIDE I), 506 ASD/548 TC across 17 sites
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with the CC200 atlas; an Extra-Trees attention mechanism selected the top 1935 connectivity features, classified with a linear SVM; evaluated with pooled 10-fold cross-validation (nested CV for hyperparameters) and a supplementary intra-site stratified shuffle-split cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: 72.2% accuracy (68.6-68.8% sensitivity, 75.4% specificity) in pooled 10-fold CV, versus 67.7% mean accuracy (66.3% sensitivity, 68.9% specificity) under the intra-site evaluation; informative connections implicated social-cognition regions and reduced anterior-posterior DMN correlation in autism.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Exclusion rule limited to missing imaging data with no motion/QC threshold; diagnosis source not reported; feature selection appears to precede the cross-validation split, raising a leakage concern; pooled-CV accuracy exceeds the site-stratified accuracy, consistent with some site leakage.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A CC200/C-PAC predictive study with a clearly reported N and pipeline but an apparent feature-selection leakage gap and only a partial (non-leave-site-out) site-handling check.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs NC); ABIDE-I, single NYU site only, 79 ASD / 105 NC (full ABIDE-I: 539 ASD/573 TC across 17 sites)
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; group-ICA identified eight brain functional networks, subject-specific spatial maps via dual regression, classified with a modified 3-D VGG-Net with squeeze-and-excitation channel attention (MCSE-VGG); evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: MCSE-VGG achieved 77.74% accuracy (76.74% precision, 78.57% recall, F1 75.33%) versus a 69.58%-accuracy baseline; ASD showed hyperconnectivity between the salience network and DMN/central executive network and hypoconnectivity between precuneus and dorsal DMN, consistent with the under-connectivity hypothesis.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single-site design chosen to avoid cross-site heterogeneity, so no cross-site generalization evidence; no separate validation dataset; ASD and NC groups differed significantly in age and IQ; no motion/QC threshold or leakage-control statement; no code/participant list released.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A well-documented single-site ABIDE-I predictive study illustrating a deliberate site-restriction strategy as an alternative to multi-site harmonisation.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Associational, unsupervised-clustering correspondence analysis; ABIDE (consistent with ABIDE I), 7 sites, 454 subjects with complete phenotypic data (256 HC, 166 autism, 32 Asperger’s; PDD-NOS excluded)
narrative_rows.methods: rs-fMRI parcellated into 200 CC200 ROIs; static/dynamic functional and effective connectivity features selected via a genetic algorithm (compared against SFS and an in-house SFR method) to maximize similarity between connectivity-derived clusters (density peak clustering, OPTICS, hierarchical clustering) and clinical diagnosis or phenotypic groupings; no cross-validation during clustering.
narrative_rows.outcomes: For ASD, connectivity-based clusters matched the clinical diagnostic grouping better than the phenotypic grouping, with a peak similarity of 89.20% (GA feature selection, hierarchical clustering, 101 features, 3 clusters); no site-specific robustness check was possible for ASD because only one site had sufficient samples per group.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Preprocessing pipeline and motion/QC details deferred to an unavailable supplement; no site handling/leave-site-out evaluation for the pooled multi-site ASD analysis; no cross-validation, so similarity values reflect in-sample correspondence rather than held-out predictive performance.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Provides an ABIDE I cohort definition (454 subjects, 7 sites) and a connectivity-to-diagnosis correspondence finding (89.20% peak similarity) relevant to characterising how well unsupervised connectivity clusters recover clinical ASD groupings.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs HC); ABIDE (consistent with ABIDE I), 871 of 1112 subjects (403 ASD, 468 HC)
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with the Harvard-Oxford atlas; Fisher z-transformed Pearson connectivity, dimensionality-reduced via recursive feature elimination; a transductive population graph (nodes = imaging features, edges weighted by gender/age/acquisition site) classified with a proposed attention/skip-connection GCN (AN-GCN), evaluated with stratified 10-fold cross-validation against several GCN-based baselines.
narrative_rows.outcomes: AN-GCN achieved 96.91% accuracy and 96.86% AUC on ABIDE, far exceeding the strongest compared baseline (DS-MML, 87.62% accuracy, 92.00% AUC) and the basic GCN baseline (64.63% accuracy).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No diagnosis-source statement; feature elimination appears to precede the CV split; site/age/gender used directly as population-graph edge weights rather than controlled for, with no leave-site-out evaluation; the very high accuracy is substantially above the paper's own baselines and typical ABIDE benchmarks, suggesting possible leakage/inflation.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Illustrates a predictive, transductive population-graph GCN approach on ABIDE with a pipeline/atlas clearly reported but validation design raising leakage concerns given an unusually high accuracy.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 871 of 1112 participants (403 ASD, 468 TC) from 17 sites, after QA; subsamples of varying homogeneity also analysed (e.g. 736, 639, 420, 226 participants)
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed ABIDE I data; systematic comparison of 6 atlas/parcellation methods x 3 connectivity measures x classifiers (SVC, ridge); leave-one-site-out and intra-site cross-validation with nested CV for hyperparameters and training-set-only ROI estimation
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best inter-site accuracy 66.8% (chance 53.7%) with MSDL atlas, tangent-space embedding, l2-regularized classifiers; accuracy increases with training sample size; discriminative connections implicate Default Mode Network, pareto-insular and semantic ROI networks
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Diagnostic label source/criteria not detailed; heterogeneous site protocols; computationally very costly pipeline comparison (reported ~10 CPU-years without grid parallelization)
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Methodological benchmark paper establishing which PCP/C-PAC pipeline + atlas + classifier choices work best on the full ABIDE I release, directly informing which pipeline/atlas combinations recur in later ABIDE classification work

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 871 subjects (403 ASD, 468 controls) from 20 sites, same subset as Abraham et al. 2017
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed Harvard-Oxford ROI connectivity features; population graph with phenotypic (sex, site) edge weighting; spectral graph convolutional network with Chebyshev filters; feature selection via RFE/PCA/MLP/autoencoder compared; 10-fold stratified CV
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best result 70.4% accuracy / 0.75 AUC (K=4, phenotypic graph), exceeding ridge, random forest and MLP baselines; authors suggest ~70% may be an intrinsic ceiling for this heterogeneous dataset
narrative_rows.key_limitations: CV is stratified by class, not by site, despite known inter-site heterogeneity; the GCN's transductive design includes test-node imaging/phenotypic features in the graph during training
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A widely cited graph-based ABIDE classification method reusing the exact Abraham et al. 2017 cohort, pipeline and atlas, useful for linking methodological lineage within the dataset-publication graph

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 964 subjects (447 autism, 517 typically developing) from 16 sites
narrative_rows.methods: Custom SPM8 preprocessing pipeline; whole-brain functional connectivity over a 7266-ROI gray-matter lattice; leave-one-subject-out classifier with age, age-squared, gender, handedness and site as covariates
narrative_rows.outcomes: Maximum 60% whole-brain classification accuracy, above chance but below the ~80% previously reported for single-site classification; most discriminative connections involved default mode network, parahippocampal/fusiform gyri, insula, Wernicke area, and intraparietal sulcus; classifier score correlated with symptom severity, social function, daily living skills and verbal IQ
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Multisite heterogeneity substantially degrades classification accuracy relative to single-site results; accuracy was significantly higher for sites with longer BOLD scan durations
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An early, influential multisite ABIDE I benchmark showing that cross-site connectivity classification underperforms single-site classification, motivating later work on pipeline/atlas choice and site-aware cross-validation

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 871 subjects (403 ASD, 468 controls) from 20 sites
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed Harvard-Oxford (110-ROI) connectivity graphs; siamese graph convolutional network learning a graph-distance metric from matching/non-matching subject pairs; k-nn (k=3) classification on learned distances compared to PCA/Euclidean distance
narrative_rows.outcomes: k-nn accuracy 62.9% across all sites with the learned GCN metric vs. 51.0% with PCA/Euclidean distance (11.9-point improvement); larger per-site improvements (e.g. site 18: 90.0% vs 50.0%); AUC improvements reported per site
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Pair-based siamese training/testing with all 20 sites represented in both splits rather than held out; short conference format limits detail on diagnostic label source and on leakage control for pair construction
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A graph-metric-learning method applied to the same well-characterised 871-subject ABIDE cohort used elsewhere in this corpus, useful for linking methodological lineage in the dataset-publication graph

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 529 ASD and 573 typically developing individuals (1102 total) from 17 sites, each processed with four pipelines (CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK)
narrative_rows.methods: A single-volume image generator converts each subject's whole-brain fMRI volume into glass-brain and stat-map images; CNN and VGG16-based deep ensemble classifiers evaluated with an 85%/15% train/test split, plus per-site (unit-site) classification
narrative_rows.outcomes: Unit-site classification accuracy up to 85% (glass-brain) and 84% (stat-map) for several sites; the third deep ensemble classifier configuration performed best across all four pipelines
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single random train/test split with no cross-validation; no leave-site-out evaluation for the pooled multi-site classifier despite known site heterogeneity
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Provides a direct four-pipeline (CCS/C-PAC/DPARSF/NIAK) comparison on the same ABIDE cohort using a non-connectivity (whole-volume image) feature representation

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Associational (within-ASD symptom-severity correlation); ABIDE I; 27 ASD participants (no ABIDE controls) from 5 sites (CALTECH, CMU, PITT, UM_1, UM_2), used as a replication arm alongside a primary 13-ASD/13-control movie-watching fMRI sample
narrative_rows.methods: Custom FSL-based preprocessing with 24-parameter motion regression and framewise-displacement scrubbing; graph-theoretic subnetwork construction and scaled-inclusivity intersubject similarity; Mantel permutation test against ADI-R/ADOS score similarity
narrative_rows.outcomes: Ventro-temporal-limbic subnetwork intersubject similarity correlated significantly with ADI-R/ADOS symptom-severity similarity in the ABIDE replication cohort (p=0.0287, r=0.17), reproducing the primary movie-watching finding
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No ABIDE control group (diagnostic scores unavailable for controls), so the ABIDE arm tests a within-ASD correlation rather than a group difference; no site or age covariate adjustment reported for the pooled 5-site ABIDE sample
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An unusually well-documented example of an ABIDE subset reconstructible from the paper alone (explicit 27-subject ID list and public filtering code), useful as a high-confidence node in the dataset-publication knowledge graph

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE I; 507 male subjects (209 ASD, 298 controls) from 14 sites, FIQ- and motion-matched
narrative_rows.methods: SPM8/DPARSF preprocessing with AAL-atlas time series; Hidden Markov Model identifying 19 recurring whole-brain states; fractional occupancy, lifetime, interval-time and transition-probability statistics compared between groups with Bonferroni-corrected two-sample t-tests, with and without regressing out site and FIQ
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD subjects showed significantly decreased fractional occupancy in HMM states 4, 8, 9, 10 and increased occupancy in states 2, 3, 14, 17 relative to controls; transition-map community structure differed between ASD-related and HC-related modules
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Male-only sample limits generalisability; site effects addressed via subject matching and covariate regression rather than formal harmonisation (e.g. ComBat)
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A dynamic (HMM-based) rather than static connectivity analysis of a well-documented, site-matched ABIDE I subset, with explicit motion/FIQ inclusion thresholds and site-interaction checks

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE I; 55 ASD and 55 age-matched typical controls (apparently single-scanner/site cohort, 3T GE Signa)
narrative_rows.methods: Custom AFNI-based pipeline (3dWarpDrive motion correction, N27 atlas warping); voxelwise fractal dimension (Hurst exponent) computed over 240 TT_Daemon ROIs; Z-score thresholding and Pearson correlation with ADI-R/ADOS severity scores
narrative_rows.outcomes: Significantly decreased signal complexity (fractal dimension) in ASD in the amygdala (p=0.001), vermis (p=0.02), basal ganglia (p=0.01) and hippocampus (p=0.02); no regions showed significantly increased complexity in ASD; FD in several ROIs correlated with ADI-R/ADOS scores
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Sex ratio differs between groups without reported adjustment; no standard motion-exclusion threshold or explicit multiple-comparisons correction reported; most ASD patients were medicated and not excluded
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A non-standard (fractal-dimension) connectivity analysis method applied to an ABIDE subset, useful for linking methodological diversity within the dataset-publication knowledge graph

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE I; 605 participants (304 ASD, 301 typically developing controls) from 7 of 16 sites (UM_1, UM_2, USM, NYU, UCLA_1, OLIN, PITT) with raw, uncorrected resting-state scans
narrative_rows.methods: SPM8 realignment used to extract 6 rigid-body head-motion parameters from raw resting-state scans; Gamma-distribution noise-to-signal ratio and shape/scale parameters computed for linear and angular micro-movement speed; non-parametric distributional comparisons across sites, age groups, comorbidity and medication subgroups
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD participants show significantly excess noise-to-signal ratio and randomness in head micro-movements relative to controls, consistently across sites, worsening with comorbidity, lower IQ, and greater autism severity, and present regardless of medication status
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Diagnostic instrument/criteria for ASD/CT labels not restated; explicit multiple-comparisons correction across the many site x age x medication subgroup tests not clearly described; medication dosage and treatment duration data unavailable
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An unconventional ABIDE analysis that repurposes head-motion time series (typically treated as a nuisance to regress out) as the primary biological signal, with explicit, reconstructible per-site inclusion criteria and N

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 452 adolescents (201 ASD, 251 neurotypical) from 17 sites (primary sample), plus a 130-subject adult generalization subsample (63 ASD, 67 NT)
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI BOLD signals over AAL90 ROIs combined with an anatomical k-nearest-neighbor brain graph; Graph Signal Processing (extended Fukunaga-Koontz transform) features classified via an interpretable decision tree; Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation with inner CV for hyperparameter tuning
narrative_rows.outcomes: Averaged test accuracy up to 74.8% (m=3), significantly outperforming a structural-only (SFM) baseline and a functional-only (GFT) baseline; predictive markers implicate frontal and temporal lobe regions; framework also generalizes to an independent adult subsample with up to a 15-point accuracy gap over SFM
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No leave-site-out evaluation despite 17-site heterogeneity; diagnostic-instrument source not restated; 'structural' network is an anatomical-distance graph rather than a diffusion-derived structural connectome
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates that combining a geometric/anatomical brain graph with rs-fMRI graph-signal features improves interpretable ASD classification over single-modality baselines on a well-specified ABIDE I adolescent subset

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I+II full releases, 539/573 (ASD/TD) and 521/573 (ASD/TD) respectively, ages 5-64, sites not itemised.
narrative_rows.methods: 3D NIfTI volumes converted to 2D axial-plane image slices (MRIcron) and classified with pre-trained CNNs (VGG-16, ResNet-50) using a single train/test split.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ResNet-50 achieved 87.0% test accuracy (best model); VGG-16 achieved 63.4%; evaluated with accuracy, recall and precision.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No motion/QC rule, no connectivity pipeline or atlas, no cross-validation or site handling, and no participant-list/code availability statement.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates ABIDE I+II used as raw image data for a non-connectivity CNN classifier; cohort cannot be reconstructed beyond the aggregate N reported.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + diagnostic prediction); ABIDE I subset of 190 male children (102 ASD, 88 TD), ages 6.5-13, from KKI, NYU, UCLA and UM.
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; functional connectivity under AAL, HO, CC and Power atlases; permutation testing for group differences; linear-SVM classification with leave-one-site-out cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best atlas (HO): leave-one-site-out mean AUC 0.75±0.05, accuracy 0.71±0.06, best fold AUC 0.83; hyper-connectivity in ASD between right angular gyrus-precuneus and right frontal operculum-left IFG, plus weaker connections elsewhere.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Restricted to male children at four sites; no study-specific participant list published; feature selection not attempted so no leakage-control procedure was needed or described in detail.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A methodologically thorough ABIDE I subset analysis combining connectivity group-difference findings with a properly site-cross-validated SVM classifier; selection rule is exact enough to approximate reconstruction but no ID list is given.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, 505 ASD and 530 TC, post-QC total 1,035, split 623/308/104 train/validation/test, sites not itemised.
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; Pearson-correlation connectivity matrices from AAL, CC and EZ atlases; SSDAE+MLP hybrid deep-learning classifier with a modified Hiking Optimization Algorithm for feature selection.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Average accuracy 0.735, sensitivity 0.765, specificity 0.752 across the three atlas-based datasets; best per-atlas accuracy 83.82% (CC atlas).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single fixed train/validation/test split with no cross-validation or site handling; no explicit leakage-control statement for feature selection/pre-training; no study-specific participant list or code.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Illustrates a deep-learning feature-selection approach on ABIDE I benchmarked against a prior published split strategy (Liu et al., 2024), but with limited reproducibility detail.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, a commonly-cited 871-subject subset (403 ASD, 468 TC), sites not itemised.
narrative_rows.methods: BASC-atlas (scale 122) functional connectivity via Pearson correlation; RNN, BiRNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN and CNN-hybrid classifiers evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best model (RNN): accuracy 74.74%, sensitivity 72.95%, specificity 76.28%, comparable to or better than several prior published results on the same subset (Table 3 comparison).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No preprocessing pipeline named, no motion/QC rule, pooled 10-fold CV with no site handling, no leakage-control statement, and no code or participant-list availability.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Uses the same widely-reused 871-subject ABIDE I subset as several prior studies, enabling direct accuracy comparison, but adds no new reproducibility information.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; all 1102 ABIDE I subjects from 17 sites, CPAC filter_noglobal preprocessing, no data screening applied, ASD/TD breakdown not in extractable text.
narrative_rows.methods: AAL (116 ROIs) and CC200 atlas functional connectivity; Low Rank and Class Discriminative Representation (LRCDR) domain-adaptation method with a linear SVM; leave-one-site-out inter-site cross-validation across all 17 sites.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Mean leave-one-site-out accuracy 73.1% (AAL) and 73.4% (CC200), outperforming compared domain-adaptation and multi-site ASD identification methods; top discriminative connections were mostly inter-network RSFCs.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No ASD/TD breakdown or QC/exclusion rule in the extractable text (explicitly no data screening applied); hyperparameter-search leakage control not described; no code or participant list, only supplementary material.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a domain-adaptation approach explicitly designed to handle ABIDE I site heterogeneity via leave-one-site-out evaluation on the full unscreened release.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + diagnostic prediction); ABIDE, four TR=2s sites (NYU, SDSU, UM, USM), 147 ASD and 146 healthy controls.
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; CC200 atlas sliding-window dynamic functional connectivity (node variability) and static node strength; SVM/RF/NB/MLP classifiers with intra-site 5-fold CV and inter-site leave-one-site-out evaluation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD showed increased FC variability in regions of otherwise-low variability in controls; classification reached up to 65% accuracy (intra-site) and ~62% accuracy (inter-site leave-one-site-out, MLP).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No motion/QC threshold beyond a TR restriction; possible feature-selection leakage from choosing nodes by cross-site group differences; no code or participant-list availability.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: An early dynamic-FC approach to ABIDE combining a group-difference finding with both pooled and leave-one-site-out classification evaluation.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, a commonly-cited 871-subject subset (403 ASD, 468 HC) from 17 sites.
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs) distance-correlation connectivity structured as a heterogeneous graph; heterogeneous graph convolutional attention network (HCAN) with MLP classification, evaluated with pooled 10-fold cross-validation and supplementary per-site 5-fold cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Average ACC 82.9%, SEN 76.7%, SPE 86.6%, AUC 84.6% (10-fold CV), exceeding compared methods on the same 871-subject subset; per-site 5-fold CV mean ACC/SEN/SPE/AUC = 75.6%/72.6%/77.3%/83.0%, with performance varying notably by site (e.g. CMU n=11).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No specific motion/QC threshold; primary evaluation pools sites rather than leave-site-out; no leakage-control statement; no study-specific code or participant list.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A graph-neural-network approach on the widely-reused 871-subject ABIDE I subset, directly comparable to several prior published methods on the same subjects.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE-I, 848 of the 1112-subject, 17-site release (396 ASD, 452 HC).
narrative_rows.methods: DPARSF-preprocessed rs-fMRI; AAL-atlas (116 ROI) functional connectivity; hierarchical functional-gradient-based graph network (ASD-HNet, ROI/community/global scales); pooled 10-fold cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD-HNet achieved accuracy 73.57%, sensitivity 72.63%, specificity 74.90%, F1 71.04%, significantly outperforming eight compared methods (paired t-test p<0.05 each).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No explicit exclusion/QC rule or motion threshold for the 848-subject subset; pooled 10-fold CV with no site handling or stated leakage control.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Code is openly released, aiding reproducibility of the model though not of the exact cohort definition; benchmarked directly against several other ABIDE-I classification methods with matched or overlapping subsets.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (biomarker group-difference derivation + ROC/AUC validation); ABIDE I+II (2095 subjects, 1001 ASD/1094 TD, 33 sites) for derivation, local KMUH cohort (21 ASD, 23 TD) for validation.
narrative_rows.methods: FSL-based lab-made pipeline; dual-regression functional connectivity against the Smith09 RSN10 template; FWE-corrected two-sample t-tests to derive 30 biomarker masks (R1-R10, A1-A20); ROC/AUC and FDR-corrected correlation analyses in the local cohort against SRS/SNAP-IV scores.
narrative_rows.outcomes: DMN and executive-control-network biomarkers differed significantly between ASD and TD; DMN connectivity was weaker in ASD; DMN-derived biomarker A4 reached AUC 0.745 in the local cohort, significantly outperforming its RSN-template-only counterpart (AUC 0.590); DMN biomarkers correlated negatively with SRS severity.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No age/sex/site covariate handling when pooling ABIDE I and II across 33 sites for the derivation step; no motion-exclusion threshold reported; underlying datasets available only on reasonable request (biomarker masks/pipeline are public).
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A clear example of deriving a biomarker from the full ABIDE I+II release and testing its transfer to an independent, non-ABIDE clinical cohort, including an explicit ROC/AUC diagnostic-utility evaluation.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Mega- and meta-analysis (associational) plus SVR prediction of SRS severity; ABIDE I+II, 939 participants (440 ASD/499 HC, all male), 18 sites
narrative_rows.methods: GRETNA-preprocessed rsfMRI, sliding-window dynamic connectomes (512-node random parcellation), multilayer-Louvain modular variability, GAM mega-analysis with ComBat site harmonisation and FDR correction, site-wise meta-analysis, SVR/LOOCV prediction of SRS scores, Allen Human Brain Atlas transcriptome association.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD showed higher mean / lower SD of whole-brain modular variability than HC; regionally higher variability in default-mode regions and lower in visual cortex (FDR p<.05); modular variability predicted SRS scores (r=.16, pperm=.002); alterations correlated with ASD-risk gene expression.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Male-only sample; gene expression reference from only 5 healthy post-mortem brains; medicated individuals not excluded; cross-sectional.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Detailed, numerically explicit ABIDE I+II QC pipeline (motion, scan length, IQ, age, site size) giving a reconstructible cohort definition; demonstrates site-harmonised mega-analysis plus leave-one-site-out sensitivity check as a model for site handling.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both associational (subtype vs TDC) and predictive (ADOS/SRS regression); ABIDE II discovery (229 ASD: 79 Asperger's/58 PDD-NOS/92 Autistic, 126 TDC, 9 sites) and ABIDE I replication (n=400, 17 sites)
narrative_rows.methods: SPM12 preprocessing, voxel-wise fALFF (functional) and GM volume (structural) maps, ADOS-guided MCCAR+jICA multimodal fusion, back-reconstruction for group differences, multiple linear regression cross-cohort prediction of ADOS/SRS, leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis.
narrative_rows.outcomes: DLPFC and superior/middle temporal cortex are shared covarying regions across subtypes; each ASD subtype shows a unique subcortical fALFF alteration pattern linked to distinct ADOS subdomains; subtype-specific patterns predict symptoms only within the matching subtype when generalised from ABIDE II to ABIDE I.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Male-only sample, not generalisable to females or the general ASD population; voxel-wise fALFF rather than atlas-based connectivity; feature definition and prediction both drew on ABIDE II data before independent ABIDE I testing.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a discovery/replication design spanning ABIDE II and ABIDE I with explicit QC thresholds and code release (FIT toolbox), useful for cohort reconstructibility assessment; illustrates subtype-stratified (rather than binary ASD/TDC) analysis.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Associational; ABIDE I+II, 37 sites, 710 ASD (79% male) / 606 CTL (87% male) after QC, ages 5-64
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC v1.8.0 preprocessing, fALFF and ReHo computed per voxel then parcellated into 11 Brodmann-area ROIs matched to post-mortem RNA-seq regions; site-mean correction; age/site/sex regressed out; Fisher r-to-z difference testing between ASD and CTL correlations, combined via Fisher's method, FDR-corrected.
narrative_rows.outcomes: 415 genes differentially correlated with fALFF/ReHo between ASD and controls (Diff Cor P<0.01, CTL FDR<0.05); effect size >1.8 for ~3% of expressed genes; developmental expression trajectories of these genes altered into adulthood.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Restricted to 11 cortical regions available from rare post-mortem ASD tissue; gene-expression comparison used a further random-subsampling procedure (e.g., ASD N=360 / Healthy N=302 in the depicted analysis) distinct from the full imaging QC sample.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Large, multi-site, well-documented ABIDE I+II QC and site-correction pipeline (CPAC, Brodmann atlas) linking imaging phenotypes to transcriptomic data; code publicly released.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I+II, 35 sites, 1383 males aged 5-40 (680 ASD/703 TD)
narrative_rows.methods: Freesurfer v6.0 structural morphometry (Desikan-Killiany-Tourville) and C-PAC functional connectivity (Harvard-Oxford, 103 regions), NeuroHarmonize site harmonization, deep-learning joint-fusion feature-reduction + classification network, nested 10-fold CV, SHAP feature importance.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Joint fusion AUC 0.78±0.04 outperformed structural-only (0.66±0.05, p<0.001 vs functional) and functional-only (0.76±0.04) models; top discriminative features in Default Mode Network and Social Brain regions.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Male-only sample; site harmonization (NeuroHarmonize) fit on the entire cohort prior to the nested CV split, risking leakage of test-fold information into the harmonization model.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Participant ID list published for reproducibility; demonstrates a multimodal structural+functional ABIDE classification pipeline with named atlases for both modalities.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE-I, 17 sites, 1035 subjects (505 ASD/530 HC)
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed CC200 functional connectivity, sparse autoencoder jointly trained with a two-layer softmax DNN classifier (ASD-SAENet); 10-fold CV on whole dataset and separate per-site 5-fold CV.
narrative_rows.outcomes: 70.8% accuracy and 79.1% specificity on the whole dataset (comparable to prior state-of-the-art but faster to train); outperformed comparators on 12/17 sites with 64.42% average per-site accuracy.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Cross-validation leakage control not explicitly described; no site harmonisation or leave-one-site-out test for the pooled model; per-site models limited by small site-level sample sizes.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Benchmarks a lightweight sparse-autoencoder classifier against prior ABIDE-I deep-learning baselines (ASD-DiagNet, Heinsfeld et al.) using the same C-PAC/CC200 preprocessing, with code released on GitHub.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I (ABIDE preprocessed), 539 ASD / 573 controls (1112 total)
narrative_rows.methods: CCS-pipeline ReHo derivative volumes (voxel-wise, no atlas) fed into a 3D CNN; 70/15/15 train/val/test split with early stopping and 10-fold cross-validation; multiple data-augmentation strategies (scaling, rotation, brightness, elastic deformation) compared.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Augmentation gave only minor test-accuracy improvements (0.6-2.2 percentage points depending on strategy/stopping rule); about half of augmentation strategies reduced accuracy; training accuracy >90% indicated overfitting.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No explicit motion/QC rule, no site handling, and authors note overfitting; absolute baseline accuracy values not stated numerically in text (only relative percentage-point changes and figures).
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Uses the full ABIDE-I ABIDE-preprocessed release (CCS pipeline, ReHo) as a methodological testbed for augmentation rather than proposing a novel classifier; illustrates a predictive study with weak leakage/site-handling reporting.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, 17 sites, 1112 initial subjects QC'd to 871 (403 ASD/468 TC)
narrative_rows.methods: CPAC-preprocessed raw 4D spatio-temporal fMRI (voxel-wise, downsampled to 28x28x28x32, no atlas) fed into a stacked small-kernel 3D-CNN + GRU network (CNNG); single 8:2 train/test split; compared against CNN-MLP, DiagNet, HI-GCN, GAT, SVC and an LSTM variant.
narrative_rows.outcomes: CNNG achieved 72.46% accuracy, 74.35% sensitivity, 79.25% specificity, AUC 0.79, outperforming all deep-learning comparators tested.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single train/test split rather than cross-validation; qualitative (non-numeric) motion/QC exclusion; no site covariate, harmonisation or leave-one-site-out evaluation despite 17-site data.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Illustrative of voxel-wise spatio-temporal (non-atlas) deep-learning approaches to ABIDE classification, and of weak reporting on cross-validation/leakage/site handling relative to connectivity-matrix-based studies.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both associational (network detection) and predictive (SVM validation); single-site ABIDE I (University of Michigan), 48 ASD / 65 TC
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC preprocessing, AAL atlas (90 ROIs), Pearson correlation + Fisher Z functional connectivity, a novel statistical graph network-detection/testing algorithm to identify abnormal subnetworks, SVM (RBF/linear) leave-one-out cross-validation using the detected subnetwork features.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Two abnormal connectivity subnetworks identified (middle temporal gyrus/precuneus; emotion/empathy-linked k-partite network); SVM classification using these features achieved 89% (RBF) and 84% (linear) leave-one-out accuracy.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single ABIDE site only (acknowledged by authors as future work to extend to multiple sites/meta-analysis); classification features derived from full-sample network detection prior to cross-validation, risking leakage; no numeric motion-QC threshold reported.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a novel subnetwork-detection method on a well-characterised single ABIDE site, illustrating both an associational discovery step and a predictive validation step, useful as a methodological contrast to multi-site ABIDE classification studies.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) analysis; ABIDE-I; n=211 males (103 ASD, 108 NT) from PITT, NYU, USM.
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI mapped to Conte69 cortical surface; vertex-wise functional connectivity combined with geodesic distance to derive connectivity distance (CD); ComBat site harmonization; vertex-wise t-tests with random field theory correction.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Widespread CD reductions in ASD vs NT concentrated in transmodal/paralimbic cortex, peak effect in the limbic intrinsic network (Cohen's d=-0.159); CD correlated positively with IQ but not age or ADOS severity.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Restricted to 3 of 17 ABIDE-I sites and to males only; cross-sectional; heterogeneity in autism limits generalizability (authors' own limitation).
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a novel connectivity-distance (geodesic-weighted FC) derivative of ABIDE-I rs-fMRI, with explicit, reconstructible site/exclusion rules but no participant list.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction demo; ABIDE I Preprocessed (full release), n=539 ASD / 573 controls.
narrative_rows.methods: Whole-brain grey-matter-masked voxel-wise ReHo features (C-PAC pipeline); scikit-learn logistic regression/SVM classifier; single random balanced split-half train/test division.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ~62% classification accuracy without dimensionality reduction or feature selection.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No cross-validation, no confidence interval, no site handling, no stated QC/exclusion rule; authors themselves frame this as a software prototype/proof-of-concept rather than a validated biomarker.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A Neurohackweek software-tool report demonstrating a reusable open classifier pipeline on the full public ABIDE I Preprocessed release.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE II, KKI site only; n=42 ASD / 127 TC (ages 8-13), after excluding 14 ASD/28 TC.
narrative_rows.methods: GRETNA v2.0.0 (SPM12) preprocessing; group ICA (GIFT) to identify 7 large-scale networks; 24 AAL-template ROIs; spectral DCM effective connectivity with PEB second-level group analysis.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD children showed decreased effective connectivity among VN, DMN, cerebellum, SMN and FPN vs TC; DMN(ANG_R)-to-SMN(PreCG_L) connectivity negatively correlated with ADOS stereotyped-behavior scores.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single site (KKI); no quantitative motion threshold reported; diagnostic-label source not restated in the analysed sections.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Demonstrates effective-connectivity (spDCM/PEB) analysis of the KKI subset of ABIDE II with AAL-based ROI definition.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational), methods-illustration; ABIDE I, UCLA site only; n=41 ASD / 32 TC after motion exclusion.
narrative_rows.methods: Standard rs-fMRI preprocessing (slice-timing, motion correction, MNI registration, bandpass, smoothing); Pearson connectivity among first 90 AAL ROIs; novel empirical-Bayes local-fdr normalization applied before group comparison with fdr and NBS correction.
narrative_rows.outcomes: 44 connectivity features differed significantly (fdr q<0.1) between ASD and TC after normalization (none with raw correlations), all showing ASD hyper-connectivity across distant functional subsystems.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Single site; diagnostic criteria and motion threshold not quantitatively specified; paper's primary contribution is the statistical method, with the ABIDE analysis as one illustrative example.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Illustrates how a connectivity-normalization method changes group-difference detection on a single-site ABIDE I subset; relevant for methodological/processing comparisons in the knowledge graph rather than as a standalone clinical finding.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational), age-stratified; ABIDE I+II, all public sites; n=1,017 ASD / 1,127 TD.
narrative_rows.methods: Linear/angular head-motion speed extracted from rs-fMRI realignment parameters; bootstrapped resampling (100 subgroups of n=25); Gamma-distribution stochastic-signature analysis (NSR, MMS); Kruskal-Wallis pairwise age-group comparisons.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Involuntary head-motion statistics shift significantly with age in TD; ASD shows significantly different, non-uniform age-dependent shifts and overall elevated involuntary motor noise relative to age-matched TD.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Outcome is head-motion kinematics rather than functional connectivity; no named preprocessing pipeline for the underlying rs-fMRI; multiple-comparison correction across many pairwise tests not fully detailed; site pooled without explicit harmonisation.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: Fully reconstructible cohort (participant indices uploaded to ABIDE, code on GitHub) spanning the whole public ABIDE I+II release, useful as a QC/motion covariate reference for other connectivity studies in the knowledge graph.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + predictive/regression); ABIDE-II, GU and KK sites; n=276 (85 ASD / 191 TD), ages 8-13.
narrative_rows.methods: FSL/AFNI preprocessing; Shen 268-node functional atlas; CPM with motion/site-masked edges; leave-one-out and split-half cross-validation with permutation testing for behavioral-regulation score prediction.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD scored significantly worse than TD on all BRIEF subscales; FC-based CPM significantly predicted inhibition (rs=.23) and, at trend level, shifting (rs=.19), but not emotion control, with distinct predictive network topographies for each subdomain.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Shifting model did not survive permutation testing at the conventional threshold; no formal site harmonisation (ComBat) or leave-site-out evaluation; no study-specific code/participant list release beyond the general CPM toolbox.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A rigorous two-site ABIDE-II CPM example combining explicit motion thresholds, a named atlas, and leakage-aware leave-one-out/permutation validation — useful methodological benchmark for the knowledge graph.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE-I; n=395 ASD / 425 TD (820 total) after QC exclusions from an initial N=1112.
narrative_rows.methods: CONN toolbox preprocessing; Schaefer 200-parcel atlas; Pearson FC; Forman-Ricci and Ollivier-Ricci graph curvature computed across 49 graph densities; two-sample t-tests with FDR correction.
narrative_rows.outcomes: ASD showed significantly lower average edge Forman-Ricci curvature than TD across most graph densities, with a similar but less consistent Ollivier-Ricci pattern; region-specific differences concentrated in Default Mode and Somatomotor networks, overlapping with NIBS (TMS/tDCS) target regions in the literature.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: IQ not matched/excluded on (a deliberate choice for generalizability); diagnostic instrument not restated; no formal multi-site harmonisation.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A fully reconstructible, whole-ABIDE-I graph-curvature analysis with public FC matrices, networks and code — a strong candidate for cross-study replication in the knowledge graph.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); multi-site ABIDE; n=85 ASD / 163 matched controls (N=248).
narrative_rows.methods: Custom FSL-based rs-fMRI preprocessing; Power 264-ROI/11-RSN atlas; PCA of FC matrices; wavelet-based temporal entropy; elastic-net (10-fold CV) regression of FC on RSN entropy, diagnosis-blind, compared post hoc between groups.
narrative_rows.outcomes: FC imbalance across 11 RSNs in ASD corresponded to a weaker FC-entropy relationship than controls; the diagnosis-blind entropy-model fit differed significantly between ASD and controls and correlated with ASD symptom severity.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No named/versioned preprocessing pipeline; no site covariate/harmonisation; diagnostic instrument not restated; no code/participant-list release found.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A methodologically detailed multi-site ABIDE example linking connectivity and temporal-entropy dynamics, using an elastic-net model as an associational (not diagnostic) tool.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, 16 sites (CC200/CC400 C-PAC derivatives); n=505 ASD / 530 TDC (N=1035).
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-derived CC200/CC400 correlation matrices combined with topological features (persistence diagrams/images/landscapes); SVM, Random Forest, and hybrid NN classifiers; 5-fold stratified cross-validation with Monte-Carlo permutation significance testing.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best accuracy 69.2% using a hybrid topological+correlation 3-layer NN; improvement from topological features over correlation alone was not always statistically significant.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: No leave-site-out evaluation despite 16 pooled sites; no quantitative motion/QC threshold reported in this paper; no study-specific code/data release; authors themselves caution against overinterpreting topological-feature gains.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A self-critical benchmark of topological-data-analysis features for ABIDE ASD classification, useful as a cautionary methodological reference in the knowledge graph.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE, 3 sites (CALTECH, CMU, KKI); n=41 ASD / 41 NC (N=82).
narrative_rows.methods: DPARSF preprocessing; AAL atlas (22 DMN ROIs); BOLD time series converted to wavelet scalogram images; pretrained CNN (DenseNet201/ResNet/GoogLeNet) feature extraction; SVM/KNN classification with k-fold cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Best accuracy 85.9% (DenseNet201 + KNN), 86.5% with 10-fold cross-validation, exceeding cited prior ABIDE functional-connectivity classifiers (66.9-70.2%).
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Small sample (N=82) from only 3 sites; no motion/QC threshold reported; no leave-site-out evaluation; no code/data release.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A DMN time-frequency/CNN-transfer-learning approach to ABIDE ASD classification, with a small, modest, non-reconstructible cohort.

narrative_rows.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE-I, all 17 sites; n=505 ASD / 530 controls (N=1035) after removing subjects with missing information.
narrative_rows.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed data; AAL atlas (90 regions, 90x90 FC matrix); novel Teacher-Student deep-learning feature ranking plus Sequential Forward Feature Selection (SFFS); classifiers (LR, LD, SVM, RF, DT) evaluated with 10-fold (combined) and 5-fold (site-wise) cross-validation.
narrative_rows.outcomes: Maximum 82% 10-fold accuracy on the combined 17-site dataset (LR/LD), outperforming prior published ABIDE classifiers in the same comparison table, and outperforming state-of-the-art in 13/17 individual sites.
narrative_rows.key_limitations: Feature selection (Teacher-Student + SFFS) appears performed prior to, rather than nested within, the reported cross-validation folds (potential leakage); all 17 sites pooled with explicitly ignored site variability and no leave-site-out evaluation; no motion/QC threshold or code/data release reported.
narrative_rows.relevance_notes: A full-ABIDE-I (17-site) classification benchmark illustrating a novel feature-selection method, useful for the knowledge graph's predictive-methods comparisons but with notable risk-of-bias caveats around leakage and site pooling.

structured_abstract: Background: ABIDE I and II are the most reused open autism rs-fMRI releases. Objective: Characterise how published studies use the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I and ABIDE II) resting-state fMRI releases: which subsets and quality-control rules define the analysed cohorts, which preprocessing pipelines and parcellations are used, whether the main claim is associational (gr… Methods: OpenAlex citation searches (994 records, 268 duplicates); metadata screen; 200 open-access reports sought, 99 retrieved and assessed on full text (1 on abstract); AI-agent charting of RQ1–RQ6 and CL1–CL8 with quotes re-verified; PROBAST / JBI appraisal. Results: 74 included (54 ABIDE I, 16 I+II, 4 II); 53 predictive. 26 used site-pooled k-fold CV and 6 leave-site-out; median headline accuracy 73.3% vs 66.8%. 8 were leakage-flagged. Cohorts were exactly reconstructible in 17 papers. Conclusion: reported ABIDE accuracies mostly come from site-mixed evaluation on cohorts that cannot be rebuilt; holding sites out and publishing participant lists are the gaps.
introduction_text: ABIDE I (2014) and ABIDE II (2017) aggregate resting-state fMRI from autistic and typically developing participants across many sites, and the Preprocessed Connectomes Project released derivatives from several pipelines. This review asks how papers subset, process and evaluate these data, and whether the analysed cohort can be traced back to the release — the link a knowledge graph of dataset use needs.
conclusions_text: Most ABIDE rs-fMRI papers in this corpus make predictive claims evaluated with cross-validation that mixes sites; a minority hold sites out, and those report lower accuracies. A few subsets recur (notably ABIDE I N=871 from the Preprocessed Connectomes Project), but participant lists are rarely published, so most cohorts can be rebuilt only partly. Reporting the participant list, the QC rule and a leave-site-out result would make these claims checkable.

protocol_snapshot.title: Use of ABIDE I and II resting-state data in autism connectivity and diagnostic-prediction studies
protocol_snapshot.objective: Characterise how published studies use the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I and ABIDE II) resting-state fMRI releases: which subsets and quality-control rules define the analysed cohorts, which preprocessing pipelines and parcellations are used, whether the main claim is associational (group difference) or predictive (diagnostic classification/regression), how it is evaluated, what is found, and whether the analysed cohort can be reconstructed from released files, so that each publication can be linked to the dataset subset it used in a knowledge graph.
protocol_snapshot.pico_population: Participants from ABIDE I and/or ABIDE II (autistic individuals and typically developing controls, all ages, all contributing sites) whose resting-state fMRI data were analysed
protocol_snapshot.pico_intervention: Analysis of ABIDE resting-state functional connectivity (raw or preprocessed releases, e.g. the Preprocessed Connectomes Project) for group-difference testing or diagnostic prediction
protocol_snapshot.pico_comparison: Autistic participants versus typically developing controls (or across-site / held-out-site evaluation for prediction studies)
protocol_snapshot.pico_outcome: Reported cohort composition and selection rules; connectivity group differences (direction, networks, effect size); diagnostic prediction performance (accuracy, AUC, sensitivity/specificity with confidence intervals); reproducibility information (code, participant lists)
protocol_snapshot.inclusion_criteria: (1) Primary research article or data descriptor (peer-reviewed journal or conference paper, or preprint); (2) analyses resting-state fMRI data from ABIDE I and/or ABIDE II (stated explicitly in the methods); (3) reports either a group-difference analysis between autism and control groups or a diagnostic prediction/classification analysis, or describes the ABIDE release itself; (4) full text in English available open access.
protocol_snapshot.exclusion_criteria: (1) Reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, theses and protocols without original ABIDE analysis; (2) studies that only cite ABIDE without analysing its data; (3) studies using only structural MRI, DTI or phenotypic data from ABIDE with no resting-state functional analysis; (4) studies whose ABIDE analysis is limited to software benchmarking with no autism-vs-control analysis (e.g. registration or motion-correction method tests); (5) non-English full text; (6) full text not openly accessible.

research_questions.question: Which ABIDE release(s) and subset (N by diagnosis, sites, QC/exclusion rule) were analysed?
Which preprocessing pipeline (e.g. Preprocessed Connectomes Project CPAC/DPARSF/NIAK/CCS, strategy) and atlas/parcellation were used?
Is the main claim associational (group difference) or predictive (classification/regression)?
How was the claim evaluated (statistical model and correction; CV scheme; held-out sites)?
What is the direction and scope of the main finding (e.g. hypo/hyper-connectivity, which networks; accuracy/AUC with CI)?
Can the analysed cohort be reconstructed from released files (participant list or exact rules published)?

charting_questions: CL1 Cohort definition reported (inclusion/exclusion rules and resulting N by diagnosis)?
CL2 Motion/QC rule reported (metric and threshold, e.g. mean FD cut-off; rater QC)?
CL3 Preprocessing pipeline and version reported?
CL5 Leakage control reported (feature selection/scaling/harmonisation confined to training folds)?
CL6 Site handling reported (site covariate, harmonisation e.g. ComBat, or leave-site-out evaluation)?
